resources.string: Android will not let this app run in the background, so it cannot report where the phone is. Allowing battery use in the background is a separate setting and does not cover this.

This phone will not let the app run in the background, so it cannot report where the phone is, and there is no setting on the phone to change that. A one-time step from a computer fixes it. Commands sent by text still work.
Nothing has reached the server since %1$s: the phone has stopped the app running in the background.

Nothing has reached the server since %1$s: this phone stops apps running in the background, and there is no setting on it to change that. A one-time step from a computer fixes it. Commands sent by text still work.
The app is running, but no location has reached the server since %1$s: the phone is getting no fix. GPS needs open sky; indoors, turn on a cell or Wi-Fi source.
Sends this phone\'s location to the server you set, encrypted. Only your password can read it, and it cannot be reset.
Cell and Wi-Fi positioning asks BeaconDB and OpenCelliD, which learn roughly where you are.

There is no browser on this phone to open that with.
The command used to communicate with Whereabouts.
Empty command not allowed, using default.
Select a ringtone for the \"ring\" command.
Lock screen message:\nWhen locking the device, this message will appear on the lock screen.
Delete — the locations go too; tap again
The server wakes this phone by push to give it commands. Whereabouts has push built in. Another UnifiedPush app, such as Sunup or ntfy, can do it instead.
built in, through Mozilla\'s push service
Waiting for Mozilla\'s push service to answer. Commands will not arrive until it does.
No other push app is installed, so commands from the server will not reach this phone. Install one, such as Sunup or ntfy, or choose Built in.
No push app is registered yet. Tap Register to choose one.
Shown while Whereabouts holds its own connection to the push service open.
Keeps a connection to Mozilla\'s push service open, so the server can reach this phone.
Whereabouts checks the connectivity to the server every X hours. Set this to 0 to disable the connectivity check.
Whereabouts will notify you if the last successful connection to the server is more than X hours ago. This has no effect if the connectivity check is disabled.
Whereabouts uploads the device\'s location every X minutes.
Values below 15 minutes are not recommended.

The source(s) from which the location data is uploaded at regular intervals in the background.\nIf none is selected, no locations are uploaded regularly. (You can still use the web interface to force an upload. This requires push.)
Upload the location of this device when the battery level goes low.
This password cannot be reset, and it is the only thing that can read your locations.
At least 8 characters. It cannot be reset, and it is the only thing that can read your locations.
The password must not equal one of the commands!
Password change failed due to a network error.
Failed login attempts to the server
Someone tried to log in to your server account \"%s\". Due to multiple failed passwords, the account is now locked for 10 minutes.
Someone tried to log in to your server account \"%1$s\" at %2$s. Due to multiple failed attempts, the account is now locked for 10 minutes.
The server\'s operator has posted the following message:\n\n%s
The server you are using has version {CURRENT}, but this app requires at least {MIN}. Controlling your device via the server may not work anymore. Please upgrade your server.
The server at %1$s can no longer be reached. The last successful connection was at %2$s.
Whereabouts can regularly check whether the server is still reachable. For privacy reasons this is off by default. But for availability reasons we recommend enabling it.
Whereabouts cannot log in to your server account \"%s\". It looks like the account was deleted from the server.
At least server version {MIN} is required, but the selected server has version {CURRENT}. Continue at your own risk.
With a server you can send commands over the internet, from the server to the app. You can also view the device location on a map. For self-hosting instructions, see the website.
The username and password must not be empty.
Only if the server asks for one.
Network request failed with HTTP 401. This can happen if the server requires a registration token and the token you provided was wrong.
Your account can be moved to the server\'s protocol v2, which improves the end-to-end encryption.
Your account already uses protocol v2. There is nothing to move.
Protocol v2 needs FMD Server 0.17.0 or later.

There is a risk of data loss if the migration is interrupted. We recommend to do the following before starting the migration:\n1. Export this app\'s settings.\n2. Log in via the web interface and export your data (locations, pictures).
To start the migration, enter the password for your account.
Keep the app open until the migration has finished.
Your account has successfully been migrated to v2.
Choose what should happen with your existing data stored on the server (locations, pictures). You can either:\n1. Delete the data (fast)\n2. Migrate the data (slow)
If you migrate the data, all locations and pictures will be downloaded, decrypted with v1, re-encrypted with v2, and re-uploaded. This will take some time.
For each entry, you can choose which commands are allowed. By default, new entries are restricted to the most basic commands.
The phone numbers in this list are allowed to access Whereabouts via SMS, by texting \"%s command\".
No phone numbers yet. Add one with a button below.
The passwords in this list can be used to access Whereabouts from any phone number via SMS, by texting \"%s password command\".
Access granted! You can now use Whereabouts for 10 minutes without including the password in your messages. Any new password that you send before your current access expires will be ignored.

The passwords in this list can be used to access Whereabouts from any app that shows a notification with a \"reply\" quick action (such as messenger apps). The notification text should be \"%s password command\".
No passwords yet. Add one with the button below.
Choose a label so that you can identify the password. The password will not be shown again after you save this entry.
Decide which commands this server account is allowed to execute (and which not).

Congratulations, you have added your first contact! You can now communicate with Whereabouts by sending an SMS that starts with \"%1$s\" from the allowed phone number. For example, send \"%2$s help\" or \"%3$s flash\". When everything works, the app will respond.
Once this entry is deleted, it will no longer be able to access Whereabouts. You can re-add it later if you change your mind.
Due to a crash, the allowed contacts were reset. Please configure them again.
Your temporary Whereabouts access expired. To continue using Whereabouts, send the password again.

Whereabouts can use the BeaconDB and OpenCelliD services to get a location estimate based on the surrounding cell towers (both) and Wi-Fi networks (BeaconDB only). An internet connection is required for every location query.
Privacy: Keep in mind that BeaconDB and OpenCelliD learn your location with every query. Please see their respective privacy policies for details.
You can contribute to BeaconDB and OpenCelliD by collecting and uploading cell tower and Wi-Fi data. See the documentation for more information.
For OpenCelliD, you need to create an account on the OpenCelliD website and get your own API Access Token.
Choose a password to encrypt the exported backup.
If you leave the password empty, the backup will be unencrypted. This risks exposing sensitive settings.
Enter the password that was used to encrypt the backup.
CAUTION: Sensitive values are not included in the backup file. Therefore, if you use the following features, please manually set them up again:\n\n1. Set the delete password.
The import failed or was only partially successful. Please check the logs for details.
Do you really want to delete all log entries?
This list automatically refreshes every second.

Find your phone when it is lost: see where it is, make it ring, lock it, or, if you turn that on here, wipe it. By text message or from your server\'s web page. Most of this code is Nulide\'s, from FindMyDevice.
You need to update some settings to continue using Whereabouts. Click to open.

Unregistering failed with the following error: {ERROR}\n\nYou can continue anyway, but your account might not have been deleted from the server. If you continue, your account will be deleted locally from this device.
Cannot execute command \"%s\": You are not allowed to execute this command.
Cannot execute command \"%1$s\": The following Android permission(s) are not granted to Whereabouts: %2$s.
The device does not seem to have Bluetooth.
Get a list of Bluetooth devices that are currently nearby.
Toggle Location Services on and off

Locate the device using one or more location providers. GPS has the highest accuracy, but may not always work. The \"fused\" provider is defined by Android, and uses a combination of sources (often WiFi or cell towers). The \"cell\" provider queries the public OpenCelliD and BeaconDB services for the surrounding cell tower locations.
Cannot locate: location is turned off.
GPS coordinates will be sent soon.

Error gaining location from OpenCelliD. This can happen if the cell tower is not in the database.

Please try the following the link: %1$s

%2$s
Error gaining location from BeaconDB. This can happen if the cell tower is not in the database.\n\n%s
Getting a fresh GPS location failed. Maybe due to a timeout.
The requested location provider \"%s\" is disabled.
No last known location. Request the latest location to force a location update.
Lock the device and optionally show a message on the lockscreen. After this, biometric unlock is unavailable and your device password is required to unlock the device.
The device should now be locked.
The device should now be ringing.
Note that \"silent\" also enables Do Not Disturb mode. This is expected behaviour and is defined by Android.
The ringer mode was changed from \"%1$s\" (old) to \"%2$s\" (new).
Toggle Do Not Disturb on and off
Do Not Disturb mode turned on.
Do Not Disturb mode turned off.
Get network statistics from the device. For example, its IP address and a list of surrounding Wifi networks.
The word sent after the command, as in \"delete password\". At least 8 characters, and nothing like the server password: this one wipes the phone.
This application is supposed to work in the background. To ensure it works even when your device is in standby, you need to turn off battery optimization for this app.
Whereabouts will occasionally send you notifications, for example to warn you that someone is locating your device.

Android pauses apps that are not opened for a few months and removes their permissions. Whereabouts, however, is supposed to work in the background. After setting it up you rarely need to open it. Therefore you need to exempt Whereabouts from being paused, otherwise it may not work in a few months.
Grant write access to secure settings

This permission can only be granted with Android\'s \"pm grant\" command line tool. You can execute this command manually via the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) using a computer. You can also execute it directly on your device using root or Shizuku.\n\nUser ID: %d
Send commands to your device over SMS. E.g., text \"%s help\" to your device. Whereabouts will reply with an SMS.

Only phone numbers that are in the allowlist can send commands. To send commands from a phone number that is not in the allowlist, you can define and include a password: \"%s mypassword help\". For convenience, so that you don\'t have to re-type the password every time, this new phone number is added to a temporary allowlist for the next 10 minutes.
SMS may incur costs for both you and the person texting you. SMS requires your SIM card to be unlocked (e.g., after a reboot).

You can allow Whereabouts to read your notifications to listen for commands. Whereabouts can then reply via Android\'s built-in notification reply feature. This allows you to control Whereabouts using a messaging application of your choice, as long as it posts notifications that can be replied to. For example, you can send a Signal message \"%s mypassword help\" to your phone.
Controlling Whereabouts via notification reply requires a password to be set. Every message must contain a correct password.
The server gives you a web page to control your device and see its location. You run it yourself. Data is stored encrypted on the server, protected by your password.
Anyone who knows your username and password can log in to the server and control your device.
Using the server needs an internet connection. This can be a mobile network (thus the SIM needs to be unlocked) or WiFi.
Send commands locally from within Whereabouts to your device. This is useful for testing. Whereabouts will reply with a notification.
Notifications when Whereabouts is receiving commands
Notifications when Whereabouts is accessed is via a password
Notifications when something fails, like the connection to the server
Notifications from the in-app transport channel

The following permissions are needed for Whereabouts to run.
Without a UnifiedPush distributor app you cannot receive commands from the server.

The push URL could not be sent to the server. Therefore, you are unable to receive commands from the server. To fix this, please open the server settings and click \"Register again\" to manually renew the push registration.

This wipes all data. Afterwards you will no longer be able to communicate with the device. To prevent accidental and malicious usage, this command requires a password and it needs to be explicitly enabled in the settings.
Cannot delete: delete command is not enabled in settings.
Dry run successful, skipping the actual device deletion.
Failed to delete device due to an exception.
The device should now be deleted. Goodbye!
Whereabouts finds this phone when it is lost. How should it be reached?
A phone you trust texts this one, and it answers with where it is, or rings. Nothing else to set up.
Also a web page with a map and buttons. Needs an account on a server that you or someone you know runs.
To read a text and answer it, and to say where the phone is even when nobody is using it. Location asks twice: the second time, choose Allow all the time.
Only the numbers here can ask this phone where it is. Add your own other phone, or someone you live with.
So that it can ring loudly even when the phone is on silent. Leave these if you only want to find it.
Log in to an account on the server, or make one there. You need its address, and a password nobody else knows: it is the only thing that can read this phone\'s locations.

The Kompakt stops apps working in the background, and nothing on the phone can change that. Until a one-time step from a computer, this phone answers texts but will not send its location to the server by itself.
This phone is stopping it at the moment.
This phone is letting it run.

From a phone you trust, text this one:

%1$s locate
It answers with where it is.

%2$s ring
It rings, even on silent.

%3$s help
It lists everything else.
Or open your server\'s web page to see it on a map.
If it ever stops answering after sitting unused for a while, the Kompakt has closed it. The README\'s On a Mudita Kompakt section has the one-time fix.
Everything here can be changed in Settings, and this guide opened again from there.
